region_scene_page.compact: Golden-age hip-hop expanded the possibilities of rap records, from Public Enemy's sonic pressure to Native Tongues' jazz-colored playfulness.
region_scene_page.standard: Golden-age hip-hop expanded the possibilities of rap records, from Public Enemy's sonic pressure to Native Tongues' jazz-colored playfulness. Eric B. & Rakim's Paid in Full, Salt-N-Pepa's Push It, Public Enemy's Rebel Without a Pause, and De La Soul's Me Myself and I give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Golden-age hip-hop expanded the possibilities of rap records, from Public Enemy's sonic pressure to Native Tongues' jazz-colored playfulness. The records sound exploratory and highly authored, as if rap's vocabulary is growing in real time. Eric B. & Rakim's Paid in Full, Salt-N-Pepa's Push It, Public Enemy's Rebel Without a Pause, and De La Soul's Me Myself and I give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
